summary: London is a tight tableau-builder where you play cards to construct buildings and civic works, then periodically 'run the city' by triggering all your card effects at once for income and resources. The tension comes from balancing expansion against loans and poverty markers, since loans must be repaid and poverty quietly erodes your score.
praised: Elegant, tight design with little downtime and quick turns
Satisfying engine-building feel without excessive fiddliness
Strong sense of progression as your city tableau grows
Good length (60-90 min) for the depth it offers
Second edition's mix of card actions keeps replayability high with variable setup
criticised: Some feel the poverty/scoring mechanism is abstract and thematically thin
Card draw and available buildings can create swingy or lucky setups
Less direct player interaction than some Wallace designs, closer to parallel optimization
The 'run the city' bookkeeping can slow down with more players
Some find it a bit dry/mechanical compared to more thematic city builders

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light drafting/take-that from cards

scoring.why: Final score comes from building values, card bonuses, and end-game scoring cards, offset by poverty accumulated during play
